meta.title: Bruno Pizza — Product case study | Julien Esterbet

hero.title: Bruno Pizza — Production
hero.subtitle: A local desktop application that turns an Excel plan into an actionable workshop production flow.
hero.imageAlt: Bruno Pizza production dashboard showing quantities by variety and distributor

problem.title: From production file to workshop use
problem.body: The need is concrete: distribute pizza production across several distributors, validate imported quantities and then guide preparation variety by variety. A spreadsheet provides the data, but it is not an interface designed for the production workflow.

solution.title: A guided local business workflow
solution.intro: The application matches the Excel plan with a business catalogue and organizes work across three complementary areas.

dashboard.title: Production dashboard
dashboard.body: Excel import and validation, header, duplicate, quantity and total checks, followed by distribution by variety and distributor.

workshop.title: Workshop flow
workshop.body: Ordered recipe, picture, progress and navigation to guide preparation pizza by pizza.

settings.title: Business settings
settings.body: Local management of pizzas, ingredients, recipes, pictures and distributors.

architecture.title: A full-stack chain packaged with Electron

steps.excel: The Excel file remains the source of the production plan.
steps.react: React and TypeScript power the interface and presentation rules.
steps.express: Express exposes a strictly local API bound to 127.0.0.1.
steps.sqlite: SQLite stores the business catalogue and recipes on the machine.
steps.electron: Electron starts the backend on an available port and provides the desktop application.

decisions.title: Make local use reliable before expanding the scope

local.title: Local operation
local.body: Data, pictures and settings remain on the machine. The server is not designed to be exposed directly to the Internet.

persistence.title: Separated persistence
persistence.body: User data is stored outside installed files so an update can reuse the existing catalogue.

quality.title: Verifiable delivery
quality.body: Frontend, backend and desktop checks are grouped before release packages are built.

items.excel: Excel remains the only production source; Adial integration is not included yet.
items.trust: The application targets trusted local use and does not include the authentication required for network exposure.
items.signing: The Windows and macOS test releases are not signed yet.

next.title: An application designed for the workshop
next.body: The public repository documents the complete flow, from Excel plan import to local persistence and desktop packaging.

meta.title: My-Website — Portfolio case study | Julien Esterbet

hero.title: My-Website
hero.subtitle: A bilingual, interactive portfolio bringing together my projects, experiments and more personal work.
hero.imageAlt: My-Website homepage presenting Julien Esterbet and his full-stack positioning

problem.title: Present my work without reducing myself to a list of technologies
problem.body: My-Website is both my professional portfolio and a space for exploration. It presents products I have actually built, makes my technical decisions visible and also opens onto Web3, travel and writing. A recruiter can understand my profile quickly, while curious visitors can explore the site at several levels.

solution.title: A professional showcase that remains personal
solution.intro: The site organizes content into distinct worlds and gives each one the right format: product case study, interactive prototype, travel journal or reflection.

architecture.title: Navigation by world
architecture.body: Portfolio, Web3, travel and reflections each have their own page, local navigation and bilingual content while sharing a coherent visual identity.

media.title: Images for every screen
media.body: Portraits, screenshots and albums are served in several sizes and modern formats to preserve quality without sending original files to visitors.

quality.title: Useful interactions
quality.body: The map, globe, galleries, timelines, Web3 tools and language switch enrich the visit while preserving keyboard paths and readable alternatives.

steps.entry: Vite initializes React, internationalization and performance measurements.
steps.shell: AppShell owns the skip link, navigation, main content, loading states and global error handling.
steps.routes: Each page and its translation namespace are loaded on demand from a single route registry.
steps.domains: Home, Web3, Travel and Reflections remain organized by domain; external calls go through dedicated services.
steps.media: ResponsiveImage consumes generated manifests to select the appropriate format and width for each context.
steps.vercel: The static build targets Vercel with Node 24, reproducible installs, a real 404 and long-lived caching limited to versioned assets.

incremental.title: Continuous evolution
incremental.body: The site is a living product: projects, trips and articles can grow without requiring the entire architecture to be rebuilt.

privacy.title: Separate sources and derivatives
privacy.body: Originals remain working sources; only cleaned and optimized variants are intended for the public site.

accessibility.title: Audit before declaration
accessibility.body: RGAA work uses a criterion matrix and manual evidence. Local results do not become a compliance statement before the deployed version is checked again.

adapters.title: Isolate external dependencies
adapters.body: Email, Mapbox, RPC, price data and wallet inspection go through adapters that separate the interface from providers.

challenges.title: Bring several experiences together in one site

legacy.title: Preserve consistency
legacy.body: Very different albums, articles, tools and case studies must remain identifiable without fragmenting the overall experience.

interactive.title: Make interaction accessible
interactive.body: The globe, map, timeline, carousels, dialogs and Web3 tools require text alternatives, keyboard navigation and careful focus management.

editorial.title: Remain credible
editorial.body: Active, academic and historical projects must be named by their real status, with results limited to what the code or audits can prove.

items.delivery: Read case studies explaining the need, behaviour, architecture and trade-offs behind each project.
items.performance: Explore Web3 prototypes, inspect public addresses and understand the technical areas that interest me.
items.media: Navigate my trips through a globe, a map, a timeline and responsive photo galleries.
items.rgaa: Read longer reflections in a bilingual interface designed for keyboard navigation and small screens.

items.deployment: React and React Router structure a single-page application split into routes loaded on demand.
items.mediaDelivery: Vite produces the static build deployed on Vercel, with SEO pages generated for the main routes.
items.securityHeaders: Mapbox, blockchain RPC, price and email calls go through dedicated services rather than interface components.
items.cv: i18next powers the French and English versions, while travel and project content lives in structured data.
items.font: Vitest, Testing Library, axe-core, ESLint and TypeScript protect important behaviour before builds.
items.fieldData: Responsive media, build budgets and lazy loading control the cost of the richest pages.
